investigations.name: Flammability of Materials on the Moon
investigations.nasa: The first-ever combustion experiment to be performed on another planetary body; investigates burning materials on the Moon at its 1/6 reduced gravity level.

investigations.name: Solid Fuel Ignition and Extinction
investigations.nasa: Explores fire growth and fire safety techniques in space. NASA-STD-6001 sets a 1-g flame propagation test for spaceflight materials, which some researchers believe is not conservative in low gravity.

investigations.name: Flammability Limits At Reduced-g Experiment
investigations.nasa: Develops a methodology to correlate material flammability limits in normal gravity and microgravity, so microgravity limits can be estimated from ground data. An international team: JAXA, NASA, ESA, CNES, DLR and universities.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids
investigations.nasa: Examines the burning and extinction characteristics of a wide variety of fuel samples in microgravity.

investigations.name: Burning and Suppression of Solids-II
investigations.nasa: Continued BASS in the Microgravity Science Glovebox: solid fuel samples burned in a flow duct. Test B20 is the record MicroFire has checked cell by cell against the NASA report.

investigations.name: Spacecraft Fire Safety Demonstration (Saffire-I to -VI)
investigations.nasa: Large-scale material flammability and fire-spread experiments inside uncrewed Cygnus cargo spacecraft after they left the station.

investigations.name: Smoke Aerosol Measurement Experiment (and re-flight)
investigations.nasa: Spacecraft smoke detectors must detect different types of smoke: hydrocarbon fuels typically produce soot, and plastics produce droplets of recondensed polymer fragments.

investigations.name: Dust and Aerosol Measurement Feasibility Test
investigations.nasa: Checked that a modified P-Trak particle counter, a key component of SAME, performs properly in microgravity; the same instrument type was used to detect dust.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment
investigations.nasa: Assesses the effectiveness of inert-gas suppressants in microgravity and the most conservative estimate of the limiting oxygen index for steady combustion; the chamber atmosphere was diluted with carbon dioxide and helium.

investigations.name: Flame Extinguishment Experiment-2 and Cool Flames Investigation
investigations.nasa: Burning droplets of liquid fuel in the Combustion Integrated Rack, including cool flames.

investigations.name: Burning Rate Emulator (ACME project)
investigations.nasa: Burned gaseous fuels to study materials flammability in still atmospheres as a function of material properties.

investigations.name: Advanced Combustion via Microgravity Experiments (six experiments)
investigations.nasa: Fundamental microgravity research aimed at improving efficiency and reducing pollutant emissions in practical combustion on Earth, using one modular hardware set in the Combustion Integrated Rack.

investigations.name: Structure and Liftoff in Combustion Experiment
investigations.nasa: Coflow laminar diffusion flames, valuable because accurate numerical modelling exists for that flame configuration.

investigations.name: Smoke Point in Co-flow Experiment
investigations.nasa: Studies the mechanisms controlling the stability and extinction of jet diffusion flames, continuing Laminar Soot Processes (LSP) from STS-94.

facilities.name: Combustion Integrated Rack (CIR)
facilities.nasa: In the U.S. Destiny laboratory; its main feature is a 100-litre combustion chamber, and it is the only ISS rack dedicated to combustion. Developed by NASA Glenn; launched in November 2008 on STS-126.

facilities.name: Multi-user Droplet Combustion Apparatus (MDCA)
facilities.nasa: A multi-user facility for droplet combustion experiments, operated inside the Combustion Integrated Rack.

facilities.name: Microgravity Science Glovebox (MSG)
facilities.nasa: The enclosed ISS work volume where BASS and BASS-II burned solid samples in a flow duct.

history.title: Apollo 1
history.what: Fire erupted in the oxygen-filled spacecraft during a pre-launch test; the crew died.

history.title: Apollo 13
history.what: An oxygen tank exploded on the way to the Moon; the crew survived a life-threatening emergency.

history.title: Fire aboard Mir
history.what: An oxygen generator failure caused a fire on the Russian station during joint operations; the multinational crew survived.

history.title: Artemis II smoke alarm
history.what: A smoke alarm sounded during the crewed Artemis II flight, about 80,000 miles from home (as quoted in the challenge brief).

spinoffs.title: Firefighter air tanks
spinoffs.what: 1970s spacesuit technology adapted into lighter firefighter air tanks and breathing gear.

spinoffs.title: Smoke detector that ignores dust
spinoffs.what: A 1970s detector developed for the Space Shuttle that tells smoke from dust, cutting nuisance alarms; used in mining and industry.

spinoffs.title: Firefighter clothing
spinoffs.what: 1980s spacesuit technology applied to improve firefighters' protective clothing.

spinoffs.title: Fine-water-mist extinguishers
spinoffs.what: Developed for use on the ISS, with practical applications on Earth (challenge brief).
